title: Gromov width of the 4D l^4 ball
quantity: Gromov width c_G(U) of U={x1^4+y1^4+x2^4+y2^4<=1} in (R^4, dx1^dy1+dx2^dy2)
lower: c_G(U) >= pi: U contains the Euclidean unit ball, since sum x_i^4 <= (sum x_i^2)^2. (Trivial.)
upper: c_G(U) <= c_Z(U) = c_EHZ(U) = c0 = 4Gamma(5/4)^2/Gamma(3/2) ~ 3.7081 (arXiv 2609.37794, Thm 2 with n=2, p=4, B=D=I). Gromov width is <= every normalized capacity. The volume bound sqrt(2 Vol U) ~ 4.65 is weaker.
W: The 4D superball x1^4+y1^4+x2^4+y2^4 <= 1 contains the round unit ball, so it holds a symplectic ball of capacity pi. Its cylindrical capacity is about 3.708, and no symplectic ball can be bigger than that. Narrow the gap: embed a bigger ball, or show that no ball of capacity close to 3.708 fits.
M: Let $U=\{x_1^4+y_1^4+x_2^4+y_2^4\le1\}\subset(\mathbb R^4,\omega_0)$ and $c_G(U)=\sup\{\pi r^2: B^4(r)\hookrightarrow U\text{ symplectically}\}$. Known: $\pi\le c_G(U)\le c_0:=4\Gamma(5/4)^2/\Gamma(3/2)\approx3.7081$ (the upper bound is $c_Z(U)=c_{EHZ}(U)=c_0$). Improve either bound: give an explicit symplectic embedding of $B^4(r)$ with $\pi r^2>\pi$, or prove $c_G(U)<c_0$.
why: Strong Viterbo (all normalized capacities agree on convex bodies) is false in general, but it is open for centrally symmetric bodies. The l^4 ball is the simplest non-toric centrally symmetric body whose EHZ and cylindrical capacities are known exactly. Any upper bound below c0 would give a centrally symmetric counterexample, and each lower-bound improvement is a checkable construction.
notes: Verified Thm 2 of 2609.37794; that paper says the centrally symmetric case is unclear and never mentions Gromov width. A quick numerical search over linear symplectic ellipsoids found nothing above pi. The upper side is hard, so this is graded B.
